key_insight: APOE effects on disease and plasma proteins vary by ancestry and sex, with SNAP25 emerging as a cross-ancestry biomarker linked to APOE-ε4 dosage.
clinical_relevance: These results support ancestry-aware interpretation of APOE-based risk, especially for dementia and liver-related phenotypes, rather than assuming one-size-fits-all genetic risk estimates.
method: Phenome-wide association study of APOE genotypes in 367,757 All of Us participants across six genetic ancestry groups.
Tested APOE alleles against 2,632 phenotypes using an Alzheimer’s-disease-risk ordinal hierarchy, with adjustment for age, sex at birth, EHR length, and 16 genetic principal components.
Evaluated ε2 and ε4 dosage effects on plasma protein levels in 9,132 participants across five ancestries; assessed sex and ancestry heterogeneity.
evidence_signal: The study identified 27 APOE-associated phenotypes, including nine with ancestry-specific effects, and found SNAP25 positively associated with APOE-ε4 dosage across ancestries.
watch_item: Findings are observational and ancestry-stratified subgroup results may be sensitive to sample size, residual confounding, and unequal representation across populations.
paper_title: Phenome-wide and proteomic analysis of APOE alleles across different ancestries in the All of Us Research Program
